argument: H3: an export ban is an adverse domestic policy shock whose application (export permits, domestic-supply allocations, enforcement) is at the Indonesian government's discretion, so connected palm firms should lose less than unconnected peers.
referee_note: Follows directly from H3; a referee may note a blanket ban leaves less room for selective treatment than a permit regime, which weakens size but not sign. I have a vague memory of sector-level moves in planter shares after the ban; it is not about the connected gap and was not used.

argument: H3: reopening exports is a favourable domestic policy shock and connected firms are expected to gain more (e.g. earlier access to export permits under the post-ban regime).
referee_note: Sign follows from H3 as written, but this event is the reversal of the ban: if connected firms were shielded from the ban they had less to recover, which predicts a negative gap; H3's '+ for both' is hard to hold for an adverse shock and its own undoing. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H3: removing the export levy is a favourable domestic policy shock, so connected palm firms are expected to gain more than unconnected peers.
referee_note: Mechanical application of H3; the levy is a uniform per-tonne rate with no discretionary allocation, so a referee can ask what channel makes ties matter (a '0' reading is defensible). No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H1: by nominating a candidate opposed to the sitting president's camp the party puts its place in the governing coalition (ministries, access) at risk, which lowers the value of ties to it.
referee_note: A second reading exists: the nomination is the party's bid for a path into the next government, which H1 would score '+'. I judge the '-' reading stronger (certain strain on current access versus a contingent claim more than a year away), but a referee could call this ambiguous. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H3: the analog switch-off is an adverse domestic regulatory shock for incumbent broadcasters, and connected media firms are expected to be less hurt than unconnected peers.
referee_note: Sign follows from H3, but (i) the switch-off date was fixed in law long before, so the shock itself was anticipated, and (ii) the news on the day is arguably that holdout groups were made to comply, i.e. ties did not buy a delay, which points to '-' if those groups are in the connected set. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H1: joining the poll-leading candidate backed by the largest bloc of governing parties strengthens the party's path into the next government, raising the value of ties to it.
referee_note: Direction follows in one step from H1; only caveat is that the endorsement may have been partly anticipated (affects size, not sign). No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H3: a rule obliging platforms to deal with news publishers is a favourable domestic policy shock, so connected media groups are expected to gain more than unconnected peers.
referee_note: Mechanical application of H3; the benefit accrues to any recognised news publisher, so the channel through which government ties raise a firm's gain (influence over the implementing committee) needs an extra step a referee may not grant. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Two readings of similar strength: a sudden forced leadership exit destabilises the party and devalues ties to the outgoing leadership ('-'), while a successor close to the incoming president improves the party's place in the next government ('+').
referee_note: H1 does not say whether ties are to the party as an organisation or to the people who lose control of it; the direction cannot be fixed without that. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H1: a party that backed the losing candidate joining the president-elect's coalition gains a path into government, raising the value of ties to it.
referee_note: Direction follows from H1; a referee may doubt the size (a small party with a weak claim on posts) but not the sign. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: The shock is a decision of the European Commission on an EU import rule; ties to the Indonesian government do not plausibly change how much a palm firm gains, so H3's proviso fails and no gap is predicted.
referee_note: A '+' would need the extra claim that Indonesian-government ties affect EU compliance costs or exposure; that is a firm-characteristics story (size, export mix), not a connection effect. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H1: a broad cabinet that keeps the governing-coalition parties in government confirms and strengthens the coalition, raising the value of ties to it.
referee_note: The inauguration date was known and the coalition's breadth largely anticipated; and the tested set is 'all ties', which mixes ties to people entering, staying in and leaving office, so the net direction for the pooled group is weaker than H1 suggests. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Given the registered view that the fund's creation is a governance cost for SOE minority shareholders, an open-ended postponement lowers the probability or delays the cost, so state-owned firms should do better than peers.
referee_note: Follows in one step from the fixed input; a referee could add that a last-minute postponement also signals policy disorder, but that is a weaker, second-order reading. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Given the registered view, a firm launch date after a postponement raises the probability and brings forward the governance cost, so state-owned firms should do worse than peers.
referee_note: Follows in one step from the fixed input; the news content may be small if the enabling law had already made the fund near-certain (size, not sign). I have a general memory that Indonesian state-bank shares and the index were weak in Feb-Mar 2025; it was not used.

argument: The launch makes the transfer of dividend rights and control to a fund with less parliamentary oversight effective, which under the registered view is a governance cost priced by minority shareholders of state-owned firms.
referee_note: Sign follows from the fixed input; the launch date was pre-announced so much may be priced already, and the same-day leadership appointments are separate news of unknown sign. I have a general memory that Indonesian state-bank shares and the index were weak in Feb-Mar 2025; it was not used.

argument: Being named lender to a political programme can be read as a directed-lending burden imposed through state ownership ('-', in line with the governance-cost logic) or as privileged access to a government-backed business line ('+', the favourable-shock reading of H3); the hypotheses do not choose between them.
referee_note: My lean is '-' (state control used for a policy purpose at minority shareholders' expense), but that requires first judging the programme adverse, which the hypotheses and premise do not establish; a mechanical H3 reading gives '+'. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: The legal transfer completes the move of the state's shares to the fund, which under the registered view is the governance cost taking effect for state-owned firms.
referee_note: The transfer was required by a law passed a month earlier, so it carries little or no news, and it concerns four banks while the tested group is all state-owned firms; a referee may say the predicted gap is negative in sign but close to zero. I have a general memory that Indonesian bank shares and the index fell sharply in March 2025; it was not used.

argument: H3: a higher export levy is an adverse domestic policy shock, and connected palm firms are expected to be less hurt than unconnected peers.
referee_note: Mechanical application of H3; as with the 2022 levy cut, a uniform rate offers no obvious channel for differential treatment, so '0' is defensible. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: H3: seizure of plantations is discretionary enforcement, the clearest case in which government ties shield a firm, so connected palm firms should be less hurt than unconnected private groups.
referee_note: Direction follows from H3 and the channel (selective enforcement) is the standard one; the caveat is empirical, namely whether ties formed under earlier governments still protect. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Under the maintained assumption that office-holding board members are valuable, a court signal that deputy ministers may not sit as commissioners raises the chance of losing them, a cost for board_office firms.
referee_note: The sign rests on the conditional assumption; the opposite reading (political appointees are a governance burden, so removal is good news) is common in the literature. The statement was non-binding reasoning, and only the deputy-minister subset of board_office firms is affected. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Under the maintained assumption, a binding bar on deputy ministers serving as SOE commissioners means the affected firms will lose valuable office-holding board members, a cost for board_office firms.
referee_note: Same objection as the July signal (the assumption can be reversed), plus partial anticipation from that signal and a two-year transition that defers the loss; only firms with deputy-minister commissioners are directly hit. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Replacing the finance minister and four others neither clearly strengthens nor clearly weakens the governing coalition, and the pooled set of all connected firms mixes ties to those removed and those appointed, so H1 gives no net direction.
referee_note: A direction would need a view on whether the reshuffle shows presidential consolidation or weakness, and then on which ties dominate the sample: two steps. I remember a market-wide fall after the finance minister was replaced; that is not the connected gap and was not used.

argument: H2/H3: a large government deposit placed only with state banks is a favourable shock delivered through the ownership tie, so state-owned banks should do better than other banks.
referee_note: The funds carry an interest cost and an expectation that they be lent out, so if loan demand is weak the placement is a margin drag or a directed-lending burden; a referee can ask why this is scored '+' if the cooperative-lending mandate is not. I have a vague recollection of state-bank shares moving after this announcement; it was not used and the sign rests on the argument alone.

argument: H1/H2 (people ties for cabinet events): a move from the SOE portfolio to a lower-ranked ministry weakens the office-holder's place in government, lowering the value of ties to him.
referee_note: He stays in cabinet, the SOE portfolio had already lost powers to the state fund, and the new portfolio may suit a sports/media group; and the tested set is all group_conn firms, of which only one group is directly touched, so the pooled prediction is weak. No memory of any price reaction used.

argument: Turning the ministry into an agency beside the fund can be read as removing a counterweight to the fund (more of the governance cost, '-'), as separating regulator from owner (a governance gain, '+'), or as formalising what the fund's creation already did (no news).
referee_note: The fixed input covers the fund's creation, not the ministry's status; any sign needs an extra assumption about whether the ministry was a check on or a duplicate of the fund. No memory of any price reaction used.
